title: Completeness of the ordinary tensor of finite-Tor integral inputs
statement: For any scheme X and two finite-Tor constructible integral inputs K,L, the ordinary tensor of the fixed reconstruction calculus is derived complete. No completion comparison or pullback assertion is included.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.9; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099N, ordinary-operation completeness step

proof.text: For every affine open apply finiteTorAffineProjectiveCharts to both inputs. Its finite tree and common finite pro-etale chart family provide bounded finite-free-retract models P,Q for each input restriction.

On each chart apply projectiveChartOrdinaryTensorModel to obtain a bounded finite-free-retract complex V representing the ordinary restriction of the specified tensor. This is only the K-flat representative comparison and finite totalization calculation.

Apply boundedProjectiveComplex_complete to V. Transfer completeness through the representative isomorphism: the canonical-unit criterion converts it to invertibility, and naturality and cancellation of isomorphisms transfer that invertibility to the tensor restriction.

The resulting chart completeness assertions satisfy affineTreeCompleteDetection. Its finite open-closed induction and affine open descent give completeness on X. The scheme may be non-qcqs and ell need not be invertible in its residue fields.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.5: affine common models, finite totalization, projective devissage and locality, without additional residue-characteristic assumptions

Project ConstructibleTensorCompletion has additional qcqs and coefficient-invertibility hypotheses; OrdinaryCompletedIntegralPullback requires Noetherian hypotheses.     (K L : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X))
    (hK : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X K)
    (hL : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X L) :
    IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E X none
      ((IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).integralClosed.tensor.obj (K, L))
